## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). - claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.content:
1	# Refactoring backlog
2	
3	A complete, trackable catalogue of refactoring opportunities in the **production**
4	code (tests are a separate later pass). Each entry maps to a
5	[Fowler code smell](https://agilepainrelief.com/glossary/code-smells/).
6	
7	Goal is eventual full cleanup — so the tail is captured too, not just the
8	headline items. Tick items off as they land; a PR can reference an `RF-NN` id.
9	
10	## How this is ranked
11	
12	- **Tier = blast radius** (change amplification): how many files you must touch
13	  today to make one routine change. Headline → High → Medium → Low.
14	- **Correctness-risk items are hoisted** above pure tidiness at the same tier.
15	- Each entry tags the **smell**, a rough **effort** (S / M / L), and lists
16	  **sibling sites** rather than repeating the entry per location.
17	- **Out of scope (already decided, not "missed"):** image lazy-loading, signed-URL
18	  batching, and the deliberate deferral of pagination — see
19	  [ADR 0001](adr/0001-list-performance-attack-image-loading-not-pagination.md) and
20	  [ADR 0002](adr/0002-batch-receipt-signed-urls.md). Where a smell touches one of
21	  those decisions, it is cross-referenced, not re-litigated.
22	
23	## Coding preferences applied
24	
25	- **Guard clauses / early returns are good** — fixes that flatten nesting via early
26	  return are encouraged, never flagged.
27	- **Heterogeneous union return types** (`string | number | object`) are a violation;
28	  a *well-formed* discriminated union (see `validateFile()` below) is the model to
29	  copy.
30	- **`any` is a smell wherever a more precise type exists** — prefer `unknown` +
31	  narrowing, typed rows, typed DTOs. Leave `any` only where the library gives no
32	  usable type, and say so.
33	- **Forced-upstream `T | null`** (provider-imposed nullability) is flagged at low
34	  priority only.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## Tier 1 — Headline (highest change amplification)
39	
40	### RF-01 — CSV parsers duplicate the whole parse loop (Template Method gap)
41	- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code + Conditional Complexity · **Effort:** M
42	- **Where:** `src/lib/services/csvParsers/AmexParser.ts`,
43	  `EQBankParser.ts`, `PCFinancialParser.ts`, `RBCFinancialParser.ts`,
44	  `SimpliiFinancialParser.ts`, `TDBankParser.ts`, `WealthSimpleParser.ts`
45	- **Evidence:** Every parser's `parse()` repeats the identical skeleton —
46	  `removeBOM()` → `parseCSV()` → locate header → resolve column indices → row
47	  loop → `parseDate()` / `parseAmount()` / `normalizeAmount()` → validate
48	  description → `push()` → collect errors. Compare `AmexParser.ts:10-100` with
49	  `EQBankParser.ts:10-88`: structurally the same, differing only in (a) header
50	  detection, (b) column-name matching, and (c) the `invertSign` flag. `BaseCSVParser`
51	  supplies the *utilities* but never a `parse()` **template**, so each subclass
52	  re-implements the orchestration.
53	- **Fix:** Pull the orchestration into `BaseCSVParser` as a Template Method and let
54	  subclasses override only the parts that actually vary:
55	
56	  ```ts
57	  // BaseCSVParser
58	  parse(csvContent: string): CSVParseResult {
59	    const transactions: ParsedTransaction[] = [];
60	    const errors: string[] = [];
61	    const rows = this.parseCSV(this.removeBOM(csvContent));
62	    if (rows.length < 2) { errors.push('CSV file is empty or has no data rows'); return { transactions, errors }; }
63	
64	    const header = this.findHeaderRow(rows);          // hook
65	    if (!header) { errors.push(this.formatError()); return { transactions, errors }; }
66	
67	    for (let i = header.dataStart; i < rows.length; i++) {
68	      const parsed = this.parseRow(rows[i], header.columns, i, errors); // hook
69	      if (parsed) transactions.push(parsed);
70	    }
71	    return { transactions, errors };
72	  }
73	  protected abstract findHeaderRow(rows: string[][]): HeaderInfo | null;
74	  protected abstract parseRow(row: string[], cols: ColumnIndex, i: number, errors: string[]): ParsedTransaction | null;
75	  ```
76	  This removes ~400 lines of copy-paste and makes a new bank a ~20-line subclass.
77	- **Note:** Keep the per-bank sign conventions intact — see the `invertSign` /
78	  Wealth Simple `type`-column rules in `CLAUDE.md`; this is correctness-sensitive.
79	
80	### RF-02 — Date-filter glue duplicated across 4 list pages (no shared composable)
81	- [ ] **Smell:** Divergent Change / Shotgun Surgery + Duplicated Code · **Effort:** M–L
82	- **Where:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `receipts/+page.svelte`,
83	  `transactions/+page.svelte`, `reconciliation/+page.svelte`
84	- **Evidence:** All four pages repeat the same filter *glue*: `tempFilterDateFrom/To`
85	  + `urlDateFrom/To` state, an `$effect` to sync temp→URL, and
86	  `applyFilterValues()` / `clearClientFilters()`. Filter-related identifiers per
87	  page: expenses 28, receipts 15, transactions 15, reconciliation 14. The shared
88	  *logic* (URL scheme + `getValidDate` from `dateValidation`) was partly centralised
89	  in commit `0614aa6`, and there is even a spec for it —
90	  `src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` — **but no `sharedDateFilter.ts`
91	  implementation exists and nothing imports it.** The per-page glue was never
92	  extracted. Adding or changing a filter today means four parallel edits.
93	- **Fix:** Build the missing module the spec already describes — a Svelte 5
94	  rune-based composable (`src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.svelte.ts`) exposing the
95	  date-filter state + `apply` / `clear` / URL-sync, and have all four pages consume
96	  it. The orphaned spec becomes its red test.
97	- **Cross-ref:** ADR 0001 notes filters run client-side over the full in-memory list;
98	  keep that behaviour — this entry is about *where the glue lives*, not pagination.
99	
100	### RF-03 — List-page table / row / empty-state markup duplicated across 3 pages
101	- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code · **Effort:** L
102	- **Where:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `receipts/+page.svelte`,
103	  `transactions/+page.svelte`
104	- **Evidence:** The three list pages each hand-roll the same table shell — selection
105	  checkbox column, date / merchant / amount columns, an actions column, and a
106	  near-identical empty-state block. They diverge only in the row's domain column
107	  (category vs card type) and the per-row action. This is the second-largest
108	  duplication source after the parsers.
109	- **Fix:** Extract a shared `<DataTable>` / `<ListRow>` pair (or a single list shell
110	  taking column definitions + a row snippet), so a column or empty-state change is
111	  one edit. *Confidence:* file-level confirmed; exact line ranges to be pinned when
112	  the work starts.
113	
114	---
115	
116	## Tier 2 — High
117	
118	### RF-04 — `findPotentialMatches` vs `findPotentialMatchesForTransaction` are a copy-paste pair
119	- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code + Long Parameter List · **Effort:** M
120	- **Where:** `src/lib/services/ReconciliationService.ts:248` and `:366`
121	- **Evidence:** Two symmetric methods (receipt-centric vs transaction-centric) with
122	  the same 5-param signature and near-identical bodies. A change to matching logic
123	  must be mirrored in both.
124	- **Fix:** Unify into one direction-parameterised matcher, or extract the shared
125	  scoring predicate both call. Pairs with RF-06 (the tolerance params).
126	
127	### RF-05 — Long methods in the service layer
128	- [ ] **Smell:** Long Method · **Effort:** M each
129	- **Where & sizes (verified):**
130	  - `PDFExportService.generateReceiptPDF` — `175–404` (~230 lines): builds summary
131	    page, loops categories, draws text/images/tables inline. Extract
132	    `drawSummaryPage()` / `drawCategoryPage()` / `drawReceiptDetails()` / `drawTable()`.
133	  - `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate` — `173–324` (~150): validate → upload → OCR →
134	    persist in one method. Extract per responsibility (see `feedback_ocr_resilience`
135	    — keep the no-orphan-file guarantee).
136	  - `ReceiptService.splitReceipt` — `364–492` (~128).
137	  - `ReconciliationService.reconcile` — `37–152` (~115) and `performMatching` —
138	    `153–247` (~94): nested receipt→transaction loops building three result lists.
139	  - `ExpenseService.getExpenses` — `67–163` (~96).
140	- **Fix:** Extract sub-steps with intention-revealing names; favour guard clauses on
141	  the validation paths.
142	
143	### RF-06 — Matching tolerances are a Long Parameter List / Data Clump
144	- [ ] **Smell:** Long Parameter List + Data Clump · **Effort:** S · *(correctness-adjacent — hoisted)*
145	- **Where:** `ReconciliationService.ts` — `performMatching` (`153`),
146	  `findPotentialMatches` (`248`), `findPotentialMatchesForTransaction` (`366`)
147	- **Evidence:** `maxDaysDifference`, `amountTolerance`,
148	  `foreignCurrencyTolerancePercent` travel together through every signature and call
149	  site, with defaults (`?? 3`, `?? 0.01`, `?? 0.05`) scattered inline.
150	- **Fix:** Introduce a `MatchingTolerances` value object with the defaults defined
151	  once, threaded as a single param. Removes the clump and the magic numbers (RF-13)
152	  in one move, and shrinks RF-04's signatures.
153	
154	### RF-07 — Singleton vs dependency-injection split across services
155	- [ ] **Smell:** Inappropriate Static + inconsistency · **Effort:** M
156	- **Where:** Singletons via `static get()`: `ReceiptService.ts:18`,
157	  `TransactionService.ts:20`, `ReconciliationService.ts:28`. DI via constructor:
158	  `ExpenseService` (`constructor(supabase)`, `new`-ed in `CategoryDropdown.svelte:94,295`),
159	  `CategoryService`.
160	- **Evidence:** Two opposite construction patterns for peer services. The singletons
161	  reach for a module-level Supabase client (harder to mock); the DI ones take it as a
162	  param. Tests and callers must know which is which.
163	- **Fix:** Pick one — DI is the more testable target (it already works for
164	  `ExpenseService` / `CategoryService`). Migrate the three singletons to constructor
165	  injection, or document a deliberate rule if the split is intentional.
166	
167	---
168	
169	## Tier 3 — Medium
170	
171	### RF-08 — `any` where a precise type exists
172	- [ ] **Smell:** weak typing (`any`) · **Effort:** S
173	- **Where (10 production sites):** `catch (e: any)` in all CSV parsers
174	  (`AmexParser.ts:95`, `EQBankParser.ts:83`, `PCFinancialParser.ts:75`,
175	  `RBCFinancialParser.ts:96`, `SimpliiFinancialParser.ts:100`, `TDBankParser.ts:83`)
176	  and `TransactionService.ts:176,236`; `ExpenseService.ts:124`
177	  `(receipt: any)`; `CategoryService.ts:283` `updateData: any`.
178	- **Fix:** `catch (e: unknown)` + narrowing; a typed Supabase row interface for the
179	  `map` callback; a typed update DTO for `updateData`. Leave `any` only if the
180	  library gives no usable type — and annotate why at that site.
181	- **Anchor (do this, don't smell):** `ReceiptService.validateFile():158` already
182	  returns `{ ok: true } | { ok: false; message: string }` — the discriminated-union
183	  style to copy, not a smell.
184	
185	### RF-09 — Three inconsistent ways to resolve a row's Category
186	- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code / inconsistency + mild Feature Envy · **Effort:** S
187	- **Where:** `expenses/+page.svelte:1333` rebuilds a `Category` inline from
188	  `category_id` / `category_name` / `category_color`; `expenses/+page.svelte:1379`
189	  uses `categories.find(...)`; `receipts/+page.svelte:1084` and
190	  `reconciliation/+page.svelte:794` use a precomputed `categoryMap`.
191	- **Evidence:** Same conceptual operation ("get the `Category` for this row"), three
192	  implementations. The inline rebuild also hard-codes a fallback colour.
193	- **Fix:** One `resolveCategory(row, categories)` helper, or nest a
194	  `category: Category | null` on the row model so no reconstruction is needed.
195	  Pairs with the Money/Date value-object discussion (Deferred).
196	
197	### RF-10 — `ReconciliationService` does UI display massaging
198	- [ ] **Smell:** Feature Envy · **Effort:** M
199	- **Where:** `convertToDisplayRows` (`:500`) and `sortDisplayRows` (`:571`)
200	- **Evidence:** The service transforms domain `ReconciliationResult` into
201	  UI-oriented display rows and sorts them — presentation concerns leaking into the
202	  service layer.
203	- **Fix:** Move row-shaping + sort to a presenter/component layer; keep the service
204	  returning domain results.
205	
206	### RF-11 — `normalizeAmount(invertSign: boolean)` flag argument
207	- [ ] **Smell:** Flag / Boolean Argument · **Effort:** S
208	- **Where:** `BaseCSVParser.ts:234`
209	- **Evidence:** A boolean that switches behaviour, set differently per bank
210	  (`true` for Amex, `false` for the rest). Well-documented, so low harm — but it is
211	  the canonical flag-argument shape.
212	- **Fix:** Once RF-01's Template Method lands, expose sign convention as a subclass
213	  property/override (e.g. `protected expensesArePositive = false`) rather than a
214	  call-site boolean. Low priority; do it *with* RF-01, not separately.
215	
216	---
217	
218	## Tier 4 — Low
219	
220	### RF-12 — Magic-number matching defaults
221	- [ ] **Smell:** Primitive Obsession (magic numbers) · **Effort:** S
222	- **Where:** `ReconciliationService.ts` — `?? 3`, `?? 0.01`, `?? 0.05` inline.

# Refactoring backlog

A complete, trackable catalogue of refactoring opportunities in the **production**
code (tests are a separate later pass). Each entry maps to a
[Fowler code smell](https://agilepainrelief.com/glossary/code-smells/).

Goal is eventual full cleanup — so the tail is captured too, not just the
headline items. Tick items off as they land; a PR can reference an `RF-NN` id.

## How this is ranked

- **Tier = blast radius** (change amplification): how many files you must touch
  today to make one routine change. Headline → High → Medium → Low.
- **Correctness-risk items are hoisted** above pure tidiness at the same tier.
- Each entry tags the **smell**, a rough **effort** (S / M / L), and lists
  **sibling sites** rather than repeating the entry per location.
- **Out of scope (already decided, not "missed"):** image lazy-loading, signed-URL
  batching, and the deliberate deferral of pagination — see
  [ADR 0001](adr/0001-list-performance-attack-image-loading-not-pagination.md) and
  [ADR 0002](adr/0002-batch-receipt-signed-urls.md). Where a smell touches one of
  those decisions, it is cross-referenced, not re-litigated.

## Coding preferences applied

- **Guard clauses / early returns are good** — fixes that flatten nesting via early
  return are encouraged, never flagged.
- **Heterogeneous union return types** (`string | number | object`) are a violation;
  a *well-formed* discriminated union (see `validateFile()` below) is the model to
  copy.
- **`any` is a smell wherever a more precise type exists** — prefer `unknown` +
  narrowing, typed rows, typed DTOs. Leave `any` only where the library gives no
  usable type, and say so.
- **Forced-upstream `T | null`** (provider-imposed nullability) is flagged at low
  priority only.

---

## Tier 1 — Headline (highest change amplification)

### RF-01 — CSV parsers duplicate the whole parse loop (Template Method gap)
- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code + Conditional Complexity · **Effort:** M
- **Where:** `src/lib/services/csvParsers/AmexParser.ts`,
  `EQBankParser.ts`, `PCFinancialParser.ts`, `RBCFinancialParser.ts`,
  `SimpliiFinancialParser.ts`, `TDBankParser.ts`, `WealthSimpleParser.ts`
- **Evidence:** Every parser's `parse()` repeats the identical skeleton —
  `removeBOM()` → `parseCSV()` → locate header → resolve column indices → row
  loop → `parseDate()` / `parseAmount()` / `normalizeAmount()` → validate
  description → `push()` → collect errors. Compare `AmexParser.ts:10-100` with
  `EQBankParser.ts:10-88`: structurally the same, differing only in (a) header
  detection, (b) column-name matching, and (c) the `invertSign` flag. `BaseCSVParser`
  supplies the *utilities* but never a `parse()` **template**, so each subclass
  re-implements the orchestration.
- **Fix:** Pull the orchestration into `BaseCSVParser` as a Template Method and let
  subclasses override only the parts that actually vary:

  ```ts
  // BaseCSVParser
  parse(csvContent: string): CSVParseResult {
    const transactions: ParsedTransaction[] = [];
    const errors: string[] = [];
    const rows = this.parseCSV(this.removeBOM(csvContent));
    if (rows.length < 2) { errors.push('CSV file is empty or has no data rows'); return { transactions, errors }; }

    const header = this.findHeaderRow(rows);          // hook
    if (!header) { errors.push(this.formatError()); return { transactions, errors }; }

    for (let i = header.dataStart; i < rows.length; i++) {
      const parsed = this.parseRow(rows[i], header.columns, i, errors); // hook
      if (parsed) transactions.push(parsed);
    }
    return { transactions, errors };
  }
  protected abstract findHeaderRow(rows: string[][]): HeaderInfo | null;
  protected abstract parseRow(row: string[], cols: ColumnIndex, i: number, errors: string[]): ParsedTransaction | null;
  ```
  This removes ~400 lines of copy-paste and makes a new bank a ~20-line subclass.
- **Note:** Keep the per-bank sign conventions intact — see the `invertSign` /
  Wealth Simple `type`-column rules in `CLAUDE.md`; this is correctness-sensitive.

### RF-02 — Date-filter glue duplicated across 4 list pages (no shared composable)
- [ ] **Smell:** Divergent Change / Shotgun Surgery + Duplicated Code · **Effort:** M–L
- **Where:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `receipts/+page.svelte`,
  `transactions/+page.svelte`, `reconciliation/+page.svelte`
- **Evidence:** All four pages repeat the same filter *glue*: `tempFilterDateFrom/To`
  + `urlDateFrom/To` state, an `$effect` to sync temp→URL, and
  `applyFilterValues()` / `clearClientFilters()`. Filter-related identifiers per
  page: expenses 28, receipts 15, transactions 15, reconciliation 14. The shared
  *logic* (URL scheme + `getValidDate` from `dateValidation`) was partly centralised
  in commit `0614aa6`, and there is even a spec for it —
  `src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` — **but no `sharedDateFilter.ts`
  implementation exists and nothing imports it.** The per-page glue was never
  extracted. Adding or changing a filter today means four parallel edits.
- **Fix:** Build the missing module the spec already describes — a Svelte 5
  rune-based composable (`src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.svelte.ts`) exposing the
  date-filter state + `apply` / `clear` / URL-sync, and have all four pages consume
  it. The orphaned spec becomes its red test.
- **Cross-ref:** ADR 0001 notes filters run client-side over the full in-memory list;
  keep that behaviour — this entry is about *where the glue lives*, not pagination.

### RF-03 — List-page table / row / empty-state markup duplicated across 3 pages
- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code · **Effort:** L
- **Where:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `receipts/+page.svelte`,
  `transactions/+page.svelte`
- **Evidence:** The three list pages each hand-roll the same table shell — selection
  checkbox column, date / merchant / amount columns, an actions column, and a
  near-identical empty-state block. They diverge only in the row's domain column
  (category vs card type) and the per-row action. This is the second-largest
  duplication source after the parsers.
- **Fix:** Extract a shared `<DataTable>` / `<ListRow>` pair (or a single list shell
  taking column definitions + a row snippet), so a column or empty-state change is
  one edit. *Confidence:* file-level confirmed; exact line ranges to be pinned when
  the work starts.

---

## Tier 2 — High

### RF-04 — `findPotentialMatches` vs `findPotentialMatchesForTransaction` are a copy-paste pair
- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code + Long Parameter List · **Effort:** M
- **Where:** `src/lib/services/ReconciliationService.ts:248` and `:366`
- **Evidence:** Two symmetric methods (receipt-centric vs transaction-centric) with
  the same 5-param signature and near-identical bodies. A change to matching logic
  must be mirrored in both.
- **Fix:** Unify into one direction-parameterised matcher, or extract the shared
  scoring predicate both call. Pairs with RF-06 (the tolerance params).

### RF-05 — Long methods in the service layer
- [ ] **Smell:** Long Method · **Effort:** M each
- **Where & sizes (verified):**
  - `PDFExportService.generateReceiptPDF` — `175–404` (~230 lines): builds summary
    page, loops categories, draws text/images/tables inline. Extract
    `drawSummaryPage()` / `drawCategoryPage()` / `drawReceiptDetails()` / `drawTable()`.
  - `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate` — `173–324` (~150): validate → upload → OCR →
    persist in one method. Extract per responsibility (see `feedback_ocr_resilience`
    — keep the no-orphan-file guarantee).
  - `ReceiptService.splitReceipt` — `364–492` (~128).
  - `ReconciliationService.reconcile` — `37–152` (~115) and `performMatching` —
    `153–247` (~94): nested receipt→transaction loops building three result lists.
  - `ExpenseService.getExpenses` — `67–163` (~96).
- **Fix:** Extract sub-steps with intention-revealing names; favour guard clauses on
  the validation paths.

### RF-06 — Matching tolerances are a Long Parameter List / Data Clump
- [ ] **Smell:** Long Parameter List + Data Clump · **Effort:** S · *(correctness-adjacent — hoisted)*
- **Where:** `ReconciliationService.ts` — `performMatching` (`153`),
  `findPotentialMatches` (`248`), `findPotentialMatchesForTransaction` (`366`)
- **Evidence:** `maxDaysDifference`, `amountTolerance`,
  `foreignCurrencyTolerancePercent` travel together through every signature and call
  site, with defaults (`?? 3`, `?? 0.01`, `?? 0.05`) scattered inline.
- **Fix:** Introduce a `MatchingTolerances` value object with the defaults defined
  once, threaded as a single param. Removes the clump and the magic numbers (RF-13)
  in one move, and shrinks RF-04's signatures.

### RF-07 — Singleton vs dependency-injection split across services
- [ ] **Smell:** Inappropriate Static + inconsistency · **Effort:** M
- **Where:** Singletons via `static get()`: `ReceiptService.ts:18`,
  `TransactionService.ts:20`, `ReconciliationService.ts:28`. DI via constructor:
  `ExpenseService` (`constructor(supabase)`, `new`-ed in `CategoryDropdown.svelte:94,295`),
  `CategoryService`.
- **Evidence:** Two opposite construction patterns for peer services. The singletons
  reach for a module-level Supabase client (harder to mock); the DI ones take it as a
  param. Tests and callers must know which is which.
- **Fix:** Pick one — DI is the more testable target (it already works for
  `ExpenseService` / `CategoryService`). Migrate the three singletons to constructor
  injection, or document a deliberate rule if the split is intentional.

---

## Tier 3 — Medium

### RF-08 — `any` where a precise type exists
- [ ] **Smell:** weak typing (`any`) · **Effort:** S
- **Where (10 production sites):** `catch (e: any)` in all CSV parsers
  (`AmexParser.ts:95`, `EQBankParser.ts:83`, `PCFinancialParser.ts:75`,
  `RBCFinancialParser.ts:96`, `SimpliiFinancialParser.ts:100`, `TDBankParser.ts:83`)
  and `TransactionService.ts:176,236`; `ExpenseService.ts:124`
  `(receipt: any)`; `CategoryService.ts:283` `updateData: any`.
- **Fix:** `catch (e: unknown)` + narrowing; a typed Supabase row interface for the
  `map` callback; a typed update DTO for `updateData`. Leave `any` only if the
  library gives no usable type — and annotate why at that site.
- **Anchor (do this, don't smell):** `ReceiptService.validateFile():158` already
  returns `{ ok: true } | { ok: false; message: string }` — the discriminated-union
  style to copy, not a smell.

### RF-09 — Three inconsistent ways to resolve a row's Category
- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code / inconsistency + mild Feature Envy · **Effort:** S
- **Where:** `expenses/+page.svelte:1333` rebuilds a `Category` inline from
  `category_id` / `category_name` / `category_color`; `expenses/+page.svelte:1379`
  uses `categories.find(...)`; `receipts/+page.svelte:1084` and
  `reconciliation/+page.svelte:794` use a precomputed `categoryMap`.
- **Evidence:** Same conceptual operation ("get the `Category` for this row"), three
  implementations. The inline rebuild also hard-codes a fallback colour.
- **Fix:** One `resolveCategory(row, categories)` helper, or nest a
  `category: Category | null` on the row model so no reconstruction is needed.
  Pairs with the Money/Date value-object discussion (Deferred).

### RF-10 — `ReconciliationService` does UI display massaging
- [ ] **Smell:** Feature Envy · **Effort:** M
- **Where:** `convertToDisplayRows` (`:500`) and `sortDisplayRows` (`:571`)
- **Evidence:** The service transforms domain `ReconciliationResult` into
  UI-oriented display rows and sorts them — presentation concerns leaking into the
  service layer.
- **Fix:** Move row-shaping + sort to a presenter/component layer; keep the service
  returning domain results.

### RF-11 — `normalizeAmount(invertSign: boolean)` flag argument
- [ ] **Smell:** Flag / Boolean Argument · **Effort:** S
- **Where:** `BaseCSVParser.ts:234`
- **Evidence:** A boolean that switches behaviour, set differently per bank
  (`true` for Amex, `false` for the rest). Well-documented, so low harm — but it is
  the canonical flag-argument shape.
- **Fix:** Once RF-01's Template Method lands, expose sign convention as a subclass
  property/override (e.g. `protected expensesArePositive = false`) rather than a
  call-site boolean. Low priority; do it *with* RF-01, not separately.

---

## Tier 4 — Low

### RF-12 — Magic-number matching defaults
- [ ] **Smell:** Primitive Obsession (magic numbers) · **Effort:** S
- **Where:** `ReconciliationService.ts` — `?? 3`, `?? 0.01`, `?? 0.05` inline.
- **Fix:** Named constants — folds into RF-06's value object. Listed separately only
  so it can be ticked if RF-06 is deferred.

### RF-13 — `PDFExportService.shouldEnablePDFExport` static + state object
- [ ] **Smell:** Inappropriate Static · **Effort:** S
- **Where:** `PDFExportService.ts:159`
- **Evidence:** A `static` predicate taking a 4-field `state` object — reads like UI
  state logic parked on the service. Minor.
- **Fix:** Move to the component/derived-state layer, or leave if it is genuinely
  shared pure logic. Lowest priority.

---

## Deferred — needs a decision before doing

These are real (Primitive Obsession / Data Clump) but the fix is **whole-codebase
shotgun surgery**, so they are parked for an explicit decision rather than scheduled.

### RF-D1 — `Money` value object (amount + currency + exchange rate)
- **Smell:** Primitive Obsession + Data Clump
- **Where:** `total_amount` / `currency` / `exchange_rate_to_cad` travel as a loose
  trio through the `Receipt` model, the reconciliation foreign-currency path, and the
  `formatCurrencyWithEstimate` call sites on expenses / reconciliation.
- **Trade-off:** A `Money` type is the textbook fix and would localise sign/rounding
  risk — **but introducing it touches every parser, service, and page**. For a family
  expense app that may be over-engineering. **Decision needed:** adopt `Money`, or
  consciously keep bare `number` + `currency` and accept the clump.

### RF-D2 — Typed date value object (vs ISO strings everywhere)
- **Smell:** Primitive Obsession
- **Where:** Dates flow as `'YYYY-MM-DD'` strings throughout; `toDate()` /
  `toISODateString()` / `getValidDate()` convert at the edges.
- **Trade-off:** The string convention is currently load-bearing and guarded by
  `CLAUDE.md`'s "never `new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')`" rule. A value object would add type
  safety but ripples everywhere and risks reintroducing timezone bugs if done
  carelessly. **Decision needed:** introduce a `LocalDate` wrapper, or keep the
  string + helper convention as-is.

---

## Not yet catalogued

- **Test suites** (the large `*.spec.ts` files) — a separate later pass, by
  agreement. Likely findings: duplicated arrange blocks, missing shared fixtures /
  builders, oversized spec files.

# PRD — Restore a green `npm run check` (type-check health)

- **Status:** Draft
- **Created:** 2026-07-01
- **Owner:** _unassigned_
- **Related:** [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md) (RF-01, RF-09), the
  "Not yet catalogued → Test suites" note therein.

## 1. Problem

`npm run check` (`svelte-check`) currently reports **118 errors across 24 files**.
A perpetually-red type check means:

- The signal is dead. New type regressions land unnoticed because "it's already
  red," so the tool no longer protects anyone.
- Real defects hide in the noise — several are genuine null-dereference and
  type-drift bugs in **production** code (see WS-1), not just test friction.
- Onboarding and AI-assisted edits are harder: a clean `check` is the fastest way
  to know a change is safe, and we can't offer that today.

The goal is to get `npm run check` to **0 errors** and keep it there via CI.

## 2. Scope

### In scope
The **112 errors** that are *not* owned by the CSV-parser refactor — 7 in
production code, 105 in test/spec files. Grouped into four workstreams (§5).

### Explicitly out of scope (owned by RF-01)
These are tracked and fixed as part of
[RF-01 (CSV parser Template Method)](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-01--csv-parsers-duplicate-the-whole-parse-loop-template-method-gap):

- The **6 production type errors** in `src/lib/services/csvParsers/*.ts`
  (`AmexParser.ts:92`, `EQBankParser.ts:80`, `PCFinancialParser.ts:72`,
  `RBCFinancialParser.ts:93`, `SimpliiFinancialParser.ts:97`, `TDBankParser.ts:80`):
  `normalizeAmount()` returns `number | null` but is assigned straight into
  `ParsedTransaction.amount: number`. Consolidating the assignment into the
  Template Method is the natural place to fix this.
- The **`WealthSimpleParser.parse()` missing `try/catch`** inconsistency (the other
  six parsers wrap their body; Wealth Simple does not). RF-01's shared `parse()`
  template decides once whether the orchestration is wrapped, which resolves the
  divergence for all seven parsers.

> **Dependency:** the "0 errors" success metric (§4) is only fully met once **both**
> this PRD and RF-01 have landed. This PRD clears 112; RF-01 clears the last 6.

## 3. Goals / Non-goals

**Goals**
- `npm run check` exits 0.
- Add `npm run check` as a **required CI gate** so it can't silently regress.
- Do it without weakening type safety — no blanket `any`, no `// @ts-nocheck`,
  no disabling `svelte-check`. (Consistent with the repo's "no `any` even in
  tests" preference.)

**Non-goals**
- No behavioural changes to shipping features. This is a type-correctness and
  test-fixture effort.
- Not a general test-quality refactor (dedup, oversized specs) — that remains the
  backlog's deferred "Test suites" pass, though WS-3 lays useful groundwork.
- Not the `Money` / `LocalDate` value-object work (backlog RF-D1 / RF-D2).

## 4. Success metrics

| Metric | Baseline | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run check` errors | 118 | **0** (with RF-01) / **6** (this PRD alone) |
| Files with problems | 24 | 0 |
| CI type-check gate | none | required on every PR |
| New `any` / `@ts-*` suppressions introduced | — | 0 (reviewed exceptions only) |

## 5. Error inventory & workstreams

Counts below exclude the 6 RF-01 csvParsers errors.

### By file

| File | Errors | Workstream |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `src/lib/tests/family-category-visibility.spec.ts` | 31 | WS-2 |
| `src/lib/services/ReceiptService.spec.ts` | 20 | WS-3 |
| `src/lib/services/CSVExportService.spec.ts` | 15 | WS-3 |
| `src/lib/tests/expenses-page-filters.spec.ts` | 10 | WS-4 |
| `src/lib/services/ReconciliationService.spec.ts` | 9 | WS-3 |
| `src/lib/services/PDFExportService.spec.ts` | 6 | WS-4 |
| `src/lib/services/ExpenseService.spec.ts` | 6 | WS-4 |
| `src/lib/tests/receipts-page.spec.ts` | 3 | WS-3 |
| `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` | 2 | WS-1 |
| `src/lib/services/OcrService.ts` | 2 | WS-1 |
| `src/routes/transactions/+page.svelte` | 1 | WS-1 |
| `src/lib/services/ReconciliationService.ts` | 1 | WS-1 |
| `src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts` | 1 | WS-1 |
| `src/lib/tests/reconciliation-foreign-currency.spec.ts` | 1 | WS-3 |
| `src/lib/services/__tests__/ReconciliationService.test.ts` | 1 | WS-3 |
| `src/lib/services/ReceiptService.split.spec.ts` | 1 | WS-3 |
| `src/lib/components/ReceiptImageViewer.spec.ts` | 1 | WS-4 |
| `src/lib/components/ReceiptEditModal.spec.ts` | 1 | WS-4 |
| **Total** | **112** | |

---

### WS-1 — Production type & null-safety (7 errors) · **Priority: highest**
These are in shipping code and several are real bug risks, not test noise. Fix
first and independently of the rest.

| Site | Error | Likely fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OcrService.ts:134` | `chatResponse` possibly `undefined`; `ChatCompletionResponse \| undefined` assigned to `ChatCompletionResponse` | Guard the Mistral SDK response before use; return a soft OCR failure if undefined (aligns with `feedback_ocr_resilience` — fail soft, no throw). |
| `PDFExportService.ts:406` | `Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>` not assignable to `BlobPart` (`SharedArrayBuffer` vs `ArrayBuffer`) | Normalize the buffer before `new Blob([...])` (e.g. copy into a fresh `Uint8Array`/`ArrayBuffer`); TS/lib-dom drift. |
| `ReconciliationService.ts:12` | Module `$lib/models/Reconciliation` has no exported member `DuplicateReceiptInfo` | Dead/renamed import — remove or point at the current type. |
| `expenses/+page.svelte:195,201` | Two different `Category` types — `$lib/services/CategoryService` (`color: string \| null`) vs `$lib/types/Category` (`color: string`) — are incompatible | Converge on one `Category` type (or make `color` nullable consistently). **Cross-ref [RF-09](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-09--three-inconsistent-ways-to-resolve-a-rows-category)** — the same Category-modelling inconsistency. |
| `transactions/+page.svelte:674` | `editRow` possibly `null` | Guard-clause / narrow before use. |

**Effort:** S–M. **Risk:** low, but touches shipping code → verify PDF export and
OCR paths manually after the change.

---

### WS-2 — Supabase mock returns `never` (31 errors) · **Priority: high**
All 31 errors in `family-category-visibility.spec.ts` share one root cause: the
test's Supabase client mock is untyped, so query-builder results collapse to
`never[]`. That produces both shapes seen:

- `Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'family_id' does not
  exist in type 'never[]'` (on `.insert({...})`)
- `Property 'id' does not exist on type 'never'` (on `data!.id`)

**Fix:** type the mock query builder against the generated `Database` schema (or a
narrow typed helper) so `.from(...).insert(...).select().single()` resolves to the
real row type. One shared, correctly-typed Supabase mock helper fixes the whole
file and prevents recurrence. **Effort:** M. **Risk:** low (test-only).

---

### WS-3 — Stale row / DTO fixtures vs evolved schema (~63 errors) · **Priority: high**
The `ReceiptRow`, `Expense`, and `TransactionRow` types gained and lost fields
(consistent with the Jan–Feb 2026 foreign-currency and receipt migrations), but
the fixtures were never updated. Two sub-shapes:

- **Missing new fields** — fixtures omit `exchange_rate_to_cad`, `original_filename`,
  `matched_transaction_id`, `currency`. (`ReceiptService.spec.ts`,
  `CSVExportService.spec.ts`, `receipts-page.spec.ts`,
  `reconciliation-foreign-currency.spec.ts`, `ReceiptService.split.spec.ts`.)
- **Removed/renamed fields still present** — e.g. `updated_at` not in `ReceiptRow`,
  `plaid_transaction_id` not in `TransactionRow`. (`ReconciliationService.spec.ts`,
  `ReconciliationService.test.ts`.)

**Fix:** introduce shared typed fixture **builders** — `makeReceiptRow()`,
`makeExpense()`, `makeTransactionRow()` — returning fully-typed objects with sane
defaults and per-test overrides. Migrate the affected specs to them. This both
clears the errors and gives the deferred "Test suites" backlog item its missing
shared fixtures. **Effort:** M–L. **Risk:** low (test-only), but touches many files.

---

### WS-4 — Miscellaneous spec type errors (11 errors) · **Priority: medium**
Assorted, mostly independent: implicit-`any` parameters, possibly-`null` access, a
no-overlap comparison, and an argument-type mismatch. Files: `expenses-page-filters.spec.ts`
(10), `PDFExportService.spec.ts` (6), `ExpenseService.spec.ts` (6),
`ReceiptImageViewer.spec.ts` (1), `ReceiptEditModal.spec.ts` (1). Fix per-site:
annotate params, add null guards, correct call arguments. **Effort:** S–M.
**Risk:** low.

## 6. Sequencing

1. **WS-1** first — small, highest value (production correctness), unblocks a clean
   production surface independent of test churn.
2. **WS-2** — single-file, single root cause; big count reduction (31) for modest effort.
3. **WS-3** — build the fixture builders, then migrate specs; largest slice.
4. **WS-4** — mop up the remainder.
5. **Add the CI gate** once errors reach the RF-01-only floor (6), and flip to
   "required" the moment RF-01 lands (0). Land RF-01 and this PRD in either order;
   the gate turns green only when both are done.

Each workstream is independently shippable and leaves `check` no worse than before.

## 7. Risks & mitigations

- **Masking instead of fixing** — the tempting shortcut is `any`/`@ts-ignore`. Non-goal
  by policy; reviewers should reject suppressions without a written reason.
- **Fixture builders drift again** — mitigate by deriving builder types *from* the
  real row/DTO types (so a future schema change breaks the builder, not 60 specs).
- **WS-1 touches shipping code** — manually verify PDF export and the OCR upload
  path; keep the OCR change fail-soft per `feedback_ocr_resilience`.

## 8. Open questions

- **Category type convergence (WS-1):** fix locally at the call site, or do the full
  RF-09 Category-modelling cleanup now? (Recommend: minimal local fix here, leave
  RF-09 as the structural follow-up.)
- **CI gate rollout:** block PRs immediately at the 6-error floor (allow-list the
  RF-01 files temporarily), or wait until RF-01 lands to flip the gate on? 
- **Fixture builders location:** co-locate under `src/lib/tests/` or a new
  `src/lib/tests/builders/`?

Pre-existing (the committed docs already fail Prettier), so I'll leave them matching the existing style rather than reformatting untouched lines.

## Done — RF-01 has landed

I refactored the seven CSV parsers onto a shared Template Method, which fixed both documented type issues as a natural side effect.

### What changed

**`BaseCSVParser` — new `parse()` Template Method** (`src/lib/services/csvParsers/BaseCSVParser.ts`)
- Owns the orchestration every parser used to duplicate: `removeBOM` → `parseCSV` → empty-file guard → `resolveLayout()` hook → row loop → collect, all in **one `try/catch`**.
- Two abstract hooks subclasses override: `resolveLayout()` (header detection + column matching) and `parseRow()`.
- A shared `finalizeRow()` for the single-amount banks that **consolidates the `normalizeAmount` → `amount` assignment** — this is where the null bug dies.
- Generic over a `CSVLayout` so each parser gets typed column indices.

**The 6 production type errors** (`AmexParser`, `EQBankParser`, `PCFinancialParser`, `RBCFinancialParser`, `SimpliiFinancialParser`, `TDBankParser`)
- `normalizeAmount()` returns `number | null`, but the raw amount is already null-checked before `finalizeRow`, and the helper guards the result — so `amount` lands as a plain `number`. All six `Type 'number | null' is not assignable to type 'number'` errors are gone.
- I **kept `normalizeAmount(amount, invertSign)`'s signature unchanged** so the direct `BaseCSVParser.test.ts` cases (which assert the null/`invertSign` behaviour) still pass. RF-11 (flag → subclass property) was left for a follow-up, as the backlog suggests.

**Wealth Simple missing-`try/catch`** (`WealthSimpleParser`)
- Now runs through the shared template, so it's wrapped like the other six. To preserve its distinct behaviour (header-only file → valid empty result, date→details→amount order, type-column sign, its own messages) it sets `minimumRowCount = 0` and keeps its own `parseRow`.

**Bonus:** the six parser `catch (e: any)` blocks collapse into the base `catch (e: unknown)`, partially clearing RF-08.

### Verification
- **`npm run check`: 118 → 112 errors**, 0 in `csvParsers`. This is exactly the RF-01-owned slice; the remaining 112 belong to the type-check-cleanup PRD.
- **229 parser tests + 1551 unit tests green**, 0 failures (I also updated the `TestCSVParser` helper in `BaseCSVParser.test.ts` to implement the new hooks).
- Prettier clean on all touched source; the 3 ESLint `no-useless-escape` warnings are pre-existing in an untouched regex (count actually dropped 4→3).

### Docs
- `docs/refactoring-backlog.md` — RF-01 ticked with a "Landed" note.
- `docs/prd-type-check-cleanup.md` — status note recording **the "0 errors" target is only fully met once both this PRD and RF-01 land**; RF-01 has now cleared its 6, leaving the PRD's 112.

content.text:
I have a definitive answer now, and it's backed by evidence.

## No — the existing tests are not sufficient for RF-02

The situation is materially worse than the backlog implies. Here's what I found.

### 1. No test touches the real page glue
Nothing renders or imports any of the four `+page.svelte` files. Zero tests bind to the actual `applyFilterValues()`, `clearClientFilters()`, the `$derived urlDateFrom/To`, or the `$effect` temp-sync. **You could delete or break the filter glue in all four pages and every test would stay green.** That's the opposite of the RF-01 situation, where 229 tests were pinned tightly to the parsers.

### 2. The "orphaned spec" is misnamed and gives false confidence
The backlog says `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` describes the missing module and "becomes its red test." It doesn't:
- It imports only `getValidDate` (already fully covered by `dateValidation.spec.ts`) and otherwise tests **inline copies** of URL/filter logic defined inside the spec itself.
- It references no `sharedDateFilter` module at all, and it's currently **GREEN**, not red (I ran it: 139 tests pass across the three filter specs).

So it will not exercise a composable you extract — it tests a parallel reimplementation.

### 3. The test copies disagree with each other and with production
- `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` filters via **string comparison** (`date < dateFrom`) — matches the real pages.
- `expenses-page-filters.spec.ts` filters via `new Date(e.transaction_date).getTime()` — does **not** match the real pages and violates CLAUDE.md's "never `new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')`" rule.

There's no single encoded source of truth to preserve during extraction.

### 4. Coverage is uneven, and the risky per-page divergences are exactly what's untested
The four pages are *not* identical glue — and the differences are unprotected:

| Page | Null-date rows | Filtering | Test coverage of date filter |
|---|---|---|---|
| expenses | kept (guarded) | client-side, string compare | inline copy only (wrong impl) |
| receipts | kept (guarded) | client-side, string compare | none real |
| transactions | **no guard** (type is non-null) + **server-side `afterDate`/`beforeDate` + inclusive-`dateTo` via `new Date(urlDateTo+'T12:00:00')`** | hybrid server + client | **none** |
| reconciliation | kept (guarded) + **month-based default range** | client-side | **none** |

A shared composable is precisely the thing that risks flattening transactions' non-null/server-side path and reconciliation's defaults — and nothing would catch it.

## Recommendation (same discipline as RF-01)
Before extracting, write characterization tests that bind to **real** units, not inline copies:

1. **Extract the pure pieces the composable will own** (URL read+validate, query-string build for apply/clear, the date-range predicate) into `sharedDateFilter.svelte.ts` and test *that module directly* — then repoint the misleading `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` at it and delete its inline copies.
2. **Add the missing cases**: null-date inclusion, exact-boundary (`>=`/`<=`) rows, `getValidDate` rejection feeding the filter, and the apply→URL→derived→clear round-trip.
3. **Net-new coverage for the two outliers**: transactions' server-side `afterDate`/`beforeDate` + inclusive-`dateTo`, and reconciliation's default range — otherwise the extraction can silently change them.

Want me to write that characterization test layer first (mirroring the "improved tests before refactoring" commit you did for RF-01), and then do the RF-02 extraction against it? I'd start with the pure-function tests since those are the highest-value safety net.
Write all the tests we will need in one run.
Before writing, I need the exact current behavior of the two outlier pages so the tests characterize them correctly. Let me read the precise logic.

## Answer: we validate them against the current code, run as an oracle

You're right that hand-authored expectations aren't self-proving — and my first pass had that gap. Here's how we actually know, now with evidence rather than assertion.

### The technique
The RF-02 logic isn't callable today because it's inline in the `.svelte` pages — but it *is* executable. `getValidDate` already exists and is the real function all four pages use; the rest are small expressions I lifted **verbatim** (with file:line citations) into a throwaway oracle harness, then fed the exact inputs my spec asserts. If the current code reproduces my expected values, the spec is a faithful characterization.

### The results
An 18-group oracle harness, run across `UTC`, `America/Toronto`, and `UTC−4`:

- **17/18 groups matched exactly, in every timezone** — `readDateFilter` (via real `getValidDate`), `matchesDateRange` (checked against *both* the guarded 3-page predicate and the unguarded transactions predicate, proving the consolidation is equivalence-preserving), `applyDateFilterParams`, `clearDateFilterParams`, `hasActiveDateFilter`. Those expected values are now proven, not guessed.

- **The 18th group found a real bug.** The transactions boundary code (`new Date(dateTo+'T12:00:00').toISOString()`) matched my values in realistic timezones but the harness showed it drifts at extremes — `toExclusiveEndBoundary('2025-01-31')` returns `2025-01-31` at UTC+14 and `2025-02-02` at UTC−12, both wrong. My spec pins the correct `2025-02-01`, so I've documented that the extraction must build this from Y/M/D string math, not copy the current code. That's the opposite of the failure mode you were worried about: instead of faithfully encoding a mistake, the validation surfaced one.

The oracle was a temporary harness (labeled as such) and I've removed it; the working tree now shows only the improved `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts`.

### What this proves — and its limits
- **Proven:** for the 5 glue functions, my expected values equal current behavior for the inputs tested. The extraction is now a true safety net — green will mean "matches the old pages," not "matches my assumptions."
- **Deliberate divergence (documented):** the 2 date-math helpers (`toExclusiveEndBoundary`, `defaultMonth*`) assert *corrected* TZ-safe values, since current code is buggy at the edges.
- **Still e2e's job:** these unit tests validate the pure logic. The reactive wiring (`$effect` temp-sync + `goto`) on each page remains covered by Playwright, per repo convention — the oracle doesn't prove that layer.
- **Example-based caveat:** the oracle proves equivalence over representative inputs, not exhaustively — normal for example tests. If you want it airtight, the extract step can add a short differential/property test (`extracted(x) === oracle(x)` over generated inputs) before deleting the oracle.

The backlog's Prettier warning is pre-existing (those committed docs already didn't conform — confirmed earlier); my additions match the surrounding style, and the module + spec are clean. RF-02 is complete.

## RF-02 done — date-filter glue extracted and wired

### What I built
**`src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.ts`** — the pure glue, with all four pages now delegating to it:

| Function | Replaces (was duplicated in) |
|---|---|
| `readDateFilter` | `getValidDate(...get('dateFrom'/'dateTo'))` × 4 pages |
| `matchesDateRange` | the client-side predicate × 4 (null-kept vs transactions-non-null variants collapsed into one) |
| `applyDateFilterParams` | the Apply `set`/`delete` param-building × 4 |
| `clearDateFilterParams` | the Clear `delete` param-building × 4 |
| `toExclusiveEndBoundary` | transactions' inline `new Date(to+'T12:00:00')…` bulk-delete math |
| `defaultMonthStart` / `defaultMonthEnd` | reconciliation's local `getDefaultStartDate/End` (now deleted) |

I deliberately did **not** make it a `.svelte.ts` rune composable — the repo has no rune/component test harness, so the pure logic lives in a node-testable module while each page keeps its own `$state`/`$derived`/`$effect`/`goto` wiring (repo convention).

### Verification (all green)
- **Module spec: 49/49**, and its expected values were validated against the pre-extraction page code via the oracle harness — so green here genuinely means "matches the old pages."
- **Full unit suite: 1566 passed, 0 failed** (10 skipped, pre-existing).
- **`npm run check`: 112 errors — unchanged.** Zero new type errors; the module is clean.
- **ESLint on the four pages went *down* ~10** (e.g. transactions 21→18); zero introduced. The 57 remaining are pre-existing app-wide patterns (`goto`-without-resolve, `{#each}`-without-key), out of RF-02 scope.
- Prettier clean on the module and spec.

### Two honest notes
1. **One mid-course correction:** my first pass also routed the pages' `hasActiveFilters` through a `hasActiveDateFilter` helper. That broke a source-introspection test (its regex `\$derived\(([\s\S]*?)\)` stops at the first `)`, and my nested call created one early) and was inconsistent (only 2 of 4 pages). I dropped the helper as YAGNI and reverted those two spots — the real duplication (read/predicate/apply/clear) is what got centralized.
2. **`src/lib/version.ts` shows `'0.115d' → '0.20'` in your working tree — that's not mine.** It predates my work and survived a stash/pop unchanged, so I left it untouched. If RF-02 should carry a version bump, that's your call given you already have that file edited.

Per repo rules I staged nothing and made no commit. The backlog's RF-02 entry is ticked with a "Landed" note recording the design, the oracle validation, and the timezone fix.

## Should we? Yes — but exactly one thin seam test, per your rule

Unit tests already own RF-02's correctness (49 oracle-validated cases). The one thing they **structurally can't** cover is the wiring I explicitly carved out of the module: Datepicker → `tempFilter*` `$state` → Apply → `applyDateFilterParams` → `goto` → URL → `$derived readDateFilter` → `matchesDateRange` → rendered rows (and Clear resets, and the `$effect` re-syncs). That runes+`goto`+DOM seam is precisely what Playwright should prove — nothing more.

One flow does it:
1. Load a list page with two rows a month apart.
2. Pick a `dateFrom` that excludes one row → click Apply → assert URL gained `?dateFrom=…` **and** the excluded row is gone from the DOM.
3. Click Clear → assert URL cleared **and** the row is back.

Because RF-02 routed all four pages through the same module, **one page proves the pattern**; the other three are identical delegations (add a cheap URL round-trip on them if you want belt-and-suspenders). Test body: ~20 lines.

## How difficult? The test is trivial; the *harness* is the work — and none exists

What I found digging through the e2e setup:
- **There is no working authenticated browser e2e.** `e2e/date-filter-url-preservation.spec.ts` never opens a browser — it's pure `URLSearchParams` asserts (fake e2e, and now redundant with `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts`). `demo.test.ts` only checks the unauthenticated home `<h1>`. So the difficulty is 90% one-time infrastructure. Options, cheapest first:

| Option | Effort | Fit with your rule |
|---|---|---|
| **A. `page.route()`-mock Supabase** — stub the session (localStorage token via `addInitScript`) + the ~3–4 load endpoints (`receipts`, `expense_categories`, `vendor_category_rules`, family lookup) with fixed JSON | **Medium once (~½ day), then ~20 min/page** | **Best** — we don't test the backend, just prove the UI renders+filters what it's handed |

| C. Component render via the unused vitest browser project | Medium, but no harness exists and `+page.svelte` needs `$app`/Supabase mocks anyway | No cheaper than A, less realistic |

# PRD — Playwright seam test for the shared date filter (route-mock harness)

- **Status:** Draft
- **Created:** 2026-07-01
- **Owner:** _unassigned_
- **Related:** [RF-02 (shared date filter)](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-02--date-filter-glue-duplicated-across-4-list-pages-no-shared-composable),
  `src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.ts` + its 49-case unit spec.

## 1. Problem

RF-02 extracted the date-filter logic into `sharedDateFilter.ts` and covers its
**correctness** with 49 node-unit tests (validated against the pre-extraction pages
via an oracle harness). What those tests *cannot* reach is the **wiring** on each
list page — the runes-and-navigation seam that connects the UI controls to that
tested logic:

```
Datepicker → tempFilterDate* ($state) → Apply → applyDateFilterParams → goto
   → URL → readDateFilter ($derived) → matchesDateRange → rendered rows
Clear → clearDateFilterParams → goto → URL cleared → $effect re-syncs temp
```

Today there is **no test that proves this seam is connected**, and the repo has no
harness that could host one:

- `e2e/date-filter-url-preservation.spec.ts` never opens a browser — every case is
  a pure `URLSearchParams` string assertion. It is unit logic in a Playwright
  costume; it now duplicates `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` and proves nothing about the
  UI.
- `e2e/demo.test.ts` only checks the unauthenticated home `<h1>`.
- The `tests/*.spec.ts` Playwright files are orphaned — they sit outside
  `testDir: 'e2e'`, do no auth, and never run.
- There is **no** `globalSetup`, `storageState`, auth fixture, or data seeding. The
  four list pages are auth-gated (`+layout.svelte` guards non-public routes) and
  Supabase-backed, so a page with no session/data renders a login prompt, not a
  filterable list.

The goal is a **thin, reliable Playwright seam test** for the shared date filter,
plus the minimal reusable harness needed to run it — without standing up a backend.

## 2. Scope

### In scope
- A `page.route()` + seeded-session harness that lets a Playwright test load an
  authenticated list page with deterministic, mocked Supabase data — **no live
  backend, no test credentials, no network**.
- **One** seam test on a representative list page (proposal: `/expenses`) proving the
  URL ↔ filtered-DOM ↔ Clear round-trip is wired to `sharedDateFilter`.
- Retiring `e2e/date-filter-url-preservation.spec.ts` (its logic now lives in
  `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts`).
- CI wiring so `npm run test:e2e` runs the new test.

### Out of scope
- Re-testing filter **behaviour/boundaries** (inclusive bounds, null-date rows,
  timezone math, validation, param preservation). That is owned by
  `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` and stays there — Playwright must not duplicate it.
- Standing up a real/seeded Supabase test project (that is the high-cost path this
  PRD deliberately avoids; see §7).
- E2E for any non-date feature; un-orphaning the parked `tests/*.spec.ts`. The
  harness this PRD builds *enables* those later, but they are not in scope here.
- Driving the flowbite `<Datepicker>` calendar widget (see §8 / §7).

## 3. Goals / Non-goals

**Goals**
- Prove, in a real browser, that each shared-filter function is actually attached to
  what the user sees — the piece unit tests structurally can't cover.
- Keep the test **thin and stable**: one page, one round-trip, deterministic
  fixtures, no flake.
- Leave behind a small, reusable `e2e/support/` harness (mock session + Supabase
  route stubs) that future seam tests can import.

**Non-goals**
- No boundary/edge coverage in Playwright (unit-owned).
- No assertion of backend or RLS behaviour — the mock returns fixed rows; correctness
  of the query is not under test here.
- No broad e2e suite. This is the "UI is attached" smoke layer, per the project's
  testing rule (unit owns correctness; Playwright proves wiring).

## 4. Success metrics

| Metric | Baseline | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Real browser tests exercising a list page's date filter | 0 | 1 (round-trip on `/expenses`) |
| Fake/browserless e2e specs | 1 (`date-filter-url-preservation`) | 0 (retired) |
| Reusable authed-page e2e harness | none | 1 (`e2e/support/`) |
| Flake rate of the new test (10 local runs) | — | 0 |
| Added Playwright coverage of filter **logic** | — | 0 (stays in unit) |

## 5. Design

### 5.1 The harness (`e2e/support/`)

Two composable helpers, imported by any authed-page test:

- **`seedSession(page)`** — put a valid-looking Supabase session in `localStorage`
  via `page.addInitScript(...)` **before** navigation, so `+layout.svelte`'s
  `supabase.auth.getSession()` resolves and the route guard passes.
  - The client is `createClient(PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY,
    { auth: { persistSession: true } })` (`src/lib/supabaseClient.ts`), so the
    storage key is supabase-js's default `sb-<project-ref>-auth-token`, where
    `<project-ref>` is derived from `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`. The helper must compute the
    key from the same env var the build used (see §7 env gotcha).
- **`mockSupabase(page, { receipts, ... })`** — `page.route()` the Supabase calls the
  page makes on load and return fixed JSON. Verified load surface for `/expenses`:

  | Intercept | Purpose | Fixture |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `**/auth/v1/user` (and `**/auth/v1/token*` on refresh) | `getSession()`/`getUser()` | one fake user `{ id }` |
  | `**/rest/v1/family_members*` | `getDefaultFamilyId()` | one active default membership → `family_id` |
  | `**/rest/v1/receipts*` | `ExpenseService.getExpenses()` | the seed rows (below) |
  | `**/rest/v1/expense_categories*` | category join | `[]` (uncategorized is fine) |
  | `**/rest/v1/vendor_category_rules*` | auto-categorization | `[]` |

  The exact endpoint list is confirmed by a one-off **discovery run** (`page.on(
  'request')` logging) as step 1 of implementation, so the stubs match reality rather
  than assumption.

### 5.2 The seam test (`e2e/date-filter.seam.spec.ts`)

Fixture: two receipts one month apart, e.g. `2025-01-15` and `2025-02-15`.

1. **URL → DOM (proves `readDateFilter` + `matchesDateRange` + `$derived` render):**
   `seedSession` + `mockSupabase`, then `goto('/expenses?dateFrom=2025-02-01')`.
   Assert the Jan row is absent and the Feb row is present.
2. **Clear → reset (proves `clearDateFilterParams` + `goto` + `$effect` re-sync):**
   click **Clear filters**. Assert the URL loses `dateFrom`/`dateTo` and both rows
   render again.
3. **(Stretch) DOM → URL (proves `tempFilter*` + `applyDateFilterParams` + Apply):**
   set the date input and click **Apply**; assert the URL gains `?dateFrom=…`. Gated
   on the flowbite `<Datepicker>` being drivable (see §7); if fiddly, this direction
   is deferred and tracked, not forced.

This is deliberately a single spec, ≤ ~40 lines, asserting *attachment* only —
concrete filtering rules remain the unit spec's job.

### 5.3 Retire the fake e2e
Delete `e2e/date-filter-url-preservation.spec.ts`. Its intent (pathname-preserving
URL construction) is covered by `applyDateFilterParams`/`clearDateFilterParams` unit
tests plus the new seam's URL assertions.

### 5.4 Representative-page rationale
RF-02 routed all four pages through the same module with identical wiring, so one
page's round-trip proves the pattern. Optional follow-up: a one-line
`goto('/receipts?dateFrom=…')`-and-assert smoke on the other three. If added, `log`
what is and isn't covered so "e2e passes" isn't read as full-UI coverage.

## 6. Sequencing

1. **Discovery run** — log the network + `localStorage` a real `/expenses` load makes;
   pin the exact intercepts and the session-token shape. (Timeboxed; output is the
   fixture list.)
2. **Harness** — `seedSession` + `mockSupabase` in `e2e/support/`, proven by getting
   `/expenses` to render a mocked list at all.
3. **Seam test** — steps 1–2 (round-trip); add step 3 if the Datepicker is drivable.
4. **Retire** the fake spec; ensure `npm run test:e2e` is green in CI (`webServer`
   already builds+previews; add a dummy `.env` with `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/anon key).
5. **(Optional)** URL smoke on the other three pages.

Each step is independently reviewable; stop after 3 if the optional smoke isn't wanted.

## 7. Risks & mitigations

- **Env at build time.** `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` are
  `$env/static/public` and must exist for `npm run build` in the `webServer`. Provide
  dummy values in CI; the harness derives the `localStorage` key from the same URL so
  the seeded session matches. *Mitigation:* a committed `.env.e2e` (dummy values) and
  a short note in the test README.
- **Mock drift / coupling to supabase-js internals.** The auth token endpoints and
  storage-key format are supabase-js implementation details; a client upgrade could
  shift them. *Mitigation:* keep the discovery script in `e2e/support/` to re-pin
  quickly; assert on user-visible outcomes (rows, URL), not on request internals.
- **flowbite `<Datepicker>` is awkward to drive** (calendar popover; it also doesn't
  forward `id`). *Mitigation:* make the URL→DOM→Clear round-trip the primary,
  Datepicker-free proof; treat the Apply-via-picker direction as stretch.
- **Slower/heavier than unit** (`build && preview` + browser). *Mitigation:* exactly
  one spec; `fullyParallel:false` and single worker already configured.
- **Scope creep into logic testing.** Reviewers should reject any boundary/edge
  assertions here — they belong in `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts`.

## 8. Open questions

- **Representative page:** `/expenses` (richest load surface, good exercise of the
  harness) vs `/transactions` (also has the `toExclusiveEndBoundary` bulk-delete
  path). Recommend `/expenses` for the seam; leave transactions' delete path to unit.
- **Stretch Apply-direction:** worth the flowbite `<Datepicker>` interaction cost, or
  is the URL→DOM→Clear round-trip a sufficient seam proof on its own?
- **Harness location/naming:** `e2e/support/` here; align with wherever the parked
  `tests/*.spec.ts` will eventually move if we un-orphan them.
- **Other three pages:** add the one-line URL smoke now, or defer until a second
  page's wiring diverges?

- `e2e/date-filter-url-preservation.spec.ts` never opens a browser — every case is
  a pure `URLSearchParams` string assertion. It is unit logic in a Playwright
  costume; it now duplicates `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` and proves nothing about the
  UI.
- `e2e/demo.test.ts` only checks the unauthenticated home `<h1>`.
- The `tests/*.spec.ts` Playwright files are orphaned — they sit outside
  `testDir: 'e2e'`, do no auth, and never run.
- There is **no** `globalSetup`, `storageState`, auth fixture, or data seeding. The
  four list pages are auth-gated (`+layout.svelte` guards non-public routes) and
  Supabase-backed, so a page with no session/data renders a login prompt, not a
  filterable list.

The goal is a **thin, reliable Playwright seam test** for the shared date filter,
plus the minimal reusable harness needed to run it — without standing up a backend.

## 2. Scope

### In scope
- A `page.route()` + seeded-session harness that lets a Playwright test load an
  authenticated list page with deterministic, mocked Supabase data — **no live
  backend, no test credentials, no network**.
- **One** seam test on a representative list page (proposal: `/expenses`) proving the
  URL ↔ filtered-DOM ↔ Clear round-trip is wired to `sharedDateFilter`.
- Retiring `e2e/date-filter-url-preservation.spec.ts` (its logic now lives in
  `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts`).
- CI wiring so `npm run test:e2e` runs the new test.

### Out of scope
- Re-testing filter **behaviour/boundaries** (inclusive bounds, null-date rows,
  timezone math, validation, param preservation). That is owned by
  `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` and stays there — Playwright must not duplicate it.
- Standing up a real/seeded Supabase test project (that is the high-cost path this
  PRD deliberately avoids; see §7).
- E2E for any non-date feature; un-orphaning the parked `tests/*.spec.ts`. The
  harness this PRD builds *enables* those later, but they are not in scope here.
- Driving the flowbite `<Datepicker>` calendar widget (see §8 / §7).

## 3. Goals / Non-goals

**Goals**
- Prove, in a real browser, that each shared-filter function is actually attached to
  what the user sees — the piece unit tests structurally can't cover.
- Keep the test **thin and stable**: one page, one round-trip, deterministic
  fixtures, no flake.
- Leave behind a small, reusable `e2e/support/` harness (mock session + Supabase
  route stubs) that future seam tests can import.

**Non-goals**
- No boundary/edge coverage in Playwright (unit-owned).
- No assertion of backend or RLS behaviour — the mock returns fixed rows; correctness
  of the query is not under test here.
- No broad e2e suite. This is the "UI is attached" smoke layer, per the project's
  testing rule (unit owns correctness; Playwright proves wiring).

## 4. Success metrics

| Metric | Baseline | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Real browser tests exercising a list page's date filter | 0 | 1 (round-trip on `/expenses`) |
| Fake/browserless e2e specs | 1 (`date-filter-url-preservation`) | 0 (retired) |
| Reusable authed-page e2e harness | none | 1 (`e2e/support/`) |
| Flake rate of the new test (10 local runs) | — | 0 |
| Added Playwright coverage of filter **logic** | — | 0 (stays in unit) |

## 5. Design

### 5.1 The harness (`e2e/support/`)

Two composable helpers, imported by any authed-page test:

- **`seedSession(page)`** — put a valid-looking Supabase session in `localStorage`
  via `page.addInitScript(...)` **before** navigation, so `+layout.svelte`'s
  `supabase.auth.getSession()` resolves and the route guard passes.
  - The client is `createClient(PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY,
    { auth: { persistSession: true } })` (`src/lib/supabaseClient.ts`), so the
    storage key is supabase-js's default `sb-<project-ref>-auth-token`, where
    `<project-ref>` is derived from `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`. The helper must compute the
    key from the same env var the build used (see §7 env gotcha).
- **`mockSupabase(page, { receipts, ... })`** — `page.route()` the Supabase calls the
  page makes on load and return fixed JSON. Verified load surface for `/expenses`:

  | Intercept | Purpose | Fixture |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `**/auth/v1/user` (and `**/auth/v1/token*` on refresh) | `getSession()`/`getUser()` | one fake user `{ id }` |
  | `**/rest/v1/family_members*` | `getDefaultFamilyId()` | one active default membership → `family_id` |
  | `**/rest/v1/receipts*` | `ExpenseService.getExpenses()` | the seed rows (below) |
  | `**/rest/v1/expense_categories*` | category join | `[]` (uncategorized is fine) |
  | `**/rest/v1/vendor_category_rules*` | auto-categorization | `[]` |

  The exact endpoint list is confirmed by a one-off **discovery run** (`page.on(
  'request')` logging) as step 1 of implementation, so the stubs match reality rather
  than assumption.

### 5.2 The seam test (`e2e/date-filter.seam.spec.ts`)

Fixture: two receipts one month apart, e.g. `2025-01-15` and `2025-02-15`.

1. **URL → DOM (proves `readDateFilter` + `matchesDateRange` + `$derived` render):**
   `seedSession` + `mockSupabase`, then `goto('/expenses?dateFrom=2025-02-01')`.
   Assert the Jan row is absent and the Feb row is present.
2. **Clear → reset (proves `clearDateFilterParams` + `goto` + `$effect` re-sync):**
   click **Clear filters**. Assert the URL loses `dateFrom`/`dateTo` and both rows
   render again.
3. **(Stretch) DOM → URL (proves `tempFilter*` + `applyDateFilterParams` + Apply):**
   set the date input and click **Apply**; assert the URL gains `?dateFrom=…`. Gated
   on the flowbite `<Datepicker>` being drivable (see §7); if fiddly, this direction
   is deferred and tracked, not forced.

This is deliberately a single spec, ≤ ~40 lines, asserting *attachment* only —
concrete filtering rules remain the unit spec's job.

### 5.3 Retire the fake e2e
Delete `e2e/date-filter-url-preservation.spec.ts`. Its intent (pathname-preserving
URL construction) is covered by `applyDateFilterParams`/`clearDateFilterParams` unit
tests plus the new seam's URL assertions.

### 5.4 Representative-page rationale
RF-02 routed all four pages through the same module with identical wiring, so one
page's round-trip proves the pattern. Optional follow-up: a one-line
`goto('/receipts?dateFrom=…')`-and-assert smoke on the other three. If added, `log`
what is and isn't covered so "e2e passes" isn't read as full-UI coverage.

## 6. Sequencing

1. **Discovery run** — log the network + `localStorage` a real `/expenses` load makes;
   pin the exact intercepts and the session-token shape. (Timeboxed; output is the
   fixture list.)
2. **Harness** — `seedSession` + `mockSupabase` in `e2e/support/`, proven by getting
   `/expenses` to render a mocked list at all.
3. **Seam test** — steps 1–2 (round-trip); add step 3 if the Datepicker is drivable.
4. **Retire** the fake spec; ensure `npm run test:e2e` is green in CI (`webServer`
   already builds+previews; add a dummy `.env` with `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/anon key).
5. **(Optional)** URL smoke on the other three pages.

Each step is independently reviewable; stop after 3 if the optional smoke isn't wanted.

## 7. Risks & mitigations

- **Env at build time.** `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` are
  `$env/static/public` and must exist for `npm run build` in the `webServer`. Provide
  dummy values in CI; the harness derives the `localStorage` key from the same URL so
  the seeded session matches. *Mitigation:* a committed `.env.e2e` (dummy values) and
  a short note in the test README.
- **Mock drift / coupling to supabase-js internals.** The auth token endpoints and
  storage-key format are supabase-js implementation details; a client upgrade could
  shift them. *Mitigation:* keep the discovery script in `e2e/support/` to re-pin
  quickly; assert on user-visible outcomes (rows, URL), not on request internals.
- **flowbite `<Datepicker>` is awkward to drive** (calendar popover; it also doesn't
  forward `id`). *Mitigation:* make the URL→DOM→Clear round-trip the primary,
  Datepicker-free proof; treat the Apply-via-picker direction as stretch.
- **Slower/heavier than unit** (`build && preview` + browser). *Mitigation:* exactly
  one spec; `fullyParallel:false` and single worker already configured.
- **Scope creep into logic testing.** Reviewers should reject any boundary/edge
  assertions here — they belong in `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts`.

## 8. Open questions

- **Representative page:** `/expenses` (richest load surface, good exercise of the
  harness) vs `/transactions` (also has the `toExclusiveEndBoundary` bulk-delete
  path). Recommend `/expenses` for the seam; leave transactions' delete path to unit.
- **Stretch Apply-direction:** worth the flowbite `<Datepicker>` interaction cost, or
  is the URL→DOM→Clear round-trip a sufficient seam proof on its own?
- **Harness location/naming:** `e2e/support/` here; align with wherever the parked
  `tests/*.spec.ts` will eventually move if we un-orphan them.
- **Other three pages:** add the one-line URL smoke now, or defer until a second
  page's wiring diverges?

## What the PRD says, in brief

**Problem** — RF-02's 49 unit tests own correctness; the one thing they can't reach is the runes+`goto`+DOM **wiring** on each page. No test proves that seam, and the repo has no harness to host one (the "date filter" e2e never opens a browser; no auth/seed/`storageState` exists).

**Scope** — build the minimal route-mock harness + **one** seam test on `/expenses` (URL → filtered-DOM → Clear round-trip), and retire the fake `date-filter-url-preservation.spec.ts`. Explicitly *out*: any boundary/logic re-testing in Playwright (stays in the unit spec) — this is the "prove the UI is attached" layer only, per your rule.

**Design** — grounded in the plumbing I verified:
- `seedSession(page)` seeds the supabase-js localStorage token (`sb-<ref>-auth-token`, key derived from `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`) via `addInitScript` so `+layout.svelte`'s guard passes.
- `mockSupabase(page, …)` `page.route()`s the confirmed `/expenses` load surface (`auth/v1/user`, `family_members`, `receipts`, `expense_categories`, `vendor_category_rules`) with fixed JSON — no backend.
- Seam test: seed two receipts a month apart → load `?dateFrom=2025-02-01`, assert Jan row gone / Feb present → click Clear, assert URL + rows reset. A stretch "Apply via Datepicker" direction is flagged as gated on the flowbite widget being drivable.

**Sequencing** — a timeboxed discovery run (log the real network/localStorage) first, so the stubs match reality; then harness → test → retire the fake → optional URL smoke on the other three pages.

**Risks** called out: build-time `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_*` env (dummy `.env.e2e`), coupling to supabase-js auth/storage internals, and the flowbite `<Datepicker>` interaction cost — with the URL→DOM→Clear round-trip chosen as the Datepicker-free primary proof.

Two decisions I left as **open questions** for you rather than presuming: representative page (`/expenses` vs `/transactions`), and whether the stretch Apply-direction is worth the Datepicker cost.

It's a Draft, uncommitted (per repo rules). Want me to implement Step 1–2 (the discovery run + harness) so we can de-risk the mock surface before committing to the full plan?
